steps.t: This is the Word screen. The title bar at the top show your document name.
Tap the Save icon to save your work. On a computer you can also press Ctrl + S.
These are the ribbon tabs. Each tab holds a group of related tools, like Home, Insert and Layout.
Under the tabs is the ribbon. It shows the buttons for the tab you picked.
The white area is the page. Click here and start typing.
The status bar shows your page number and word count.
Click anywhere on the white page. A blinking line appears. That is where your typing will go.
Type with the keyboard. Press Enter to start a new line or paragraph.
Press Backspace to delete the letter before the blinking line, and Delete to remove the one after it.
Drag across words to select them. Double-click one word to select just that word.
Press Ctrl + A to select everything in the document.
Click anywhere on the page to remove the selection.
Click and drag across the words you want to change. They turn blue when selected.
Click the Home tab to open the text tools.
Click B to make the selected text bold.
I makes text italic and U underlines it. Try both.
Use the size box to make text bigger or smaller.
Click the Insert tab.
The Insert ribbon is now showing. Find the Table button.
Click Table, then drag across the grid to pick how many rows and columns you need.
Let go of the mouse. Your table appears on the page, ready for typing.
Select the words you want to move. They turn blue.
Click the Center button. The text moves to the middle of the page.
Click Align Right to push the text to the right edge.
Click Align Left to bring it back. Left is the normal position for most documents.
Type each item on its own line, then drag across them to select the whole list.
Click the Bullets button on the Home tab to turn the list into bullet points.
Click Numbering instead to number the list 1, 2, 3.
Click the Insert tab.
Click Pictures to browse for a photo saved on your computer.
Choose your picture and click Insert. It appears on the page.
Made a mistake? Click Undo to take back your last action.
Click Redo to bring back what you just undid.
A faster way: hold Ctrl and press Z to undo, or Ctrl + Y to redo.
Click the Review tab.
Click Spelling. Word checks your document and shows each mistake it finds.
A red line under a word means Word thinks it is spelled wrong. Right-click it to see suggestions.
Select the words you want to change.
Click the font name box to see a list of fonts, such as Calibri, Arial and Times New Roman.
Pick a font from the list. The selected words change at once.
Justify spreads each line evenly from the left edge to the right edge, like in a book.
Select your paragraph, then click Justify.
Click Align Left again if you want the usual uneven right edge.
Select the text you want to copy.
Press Ctrl + C to copy it. Nothing seems to change, but Word has remembered the text.
Click where you want the copy to go, then click Paste on the Home tab, or press Ctrl + V.
Click the Insert tab.
Click Shapes to see rectangles, circles, arrows and more.
Choose a shape, then drag on the page to draw it.
The status bar always shows how many words you have typed.
For more detail, click the Review tab.
Click Word Count to see words, characters, paragraphs and lines.
Select a word you want to replace.
Click the Review tab, then click Thesaurus.
Word shows words with a similar meaning. Click one to use it.
Zoom makes the page look bigger or smaller without changing your document.
Slide to the right to zoom in, and to the left to zoom out.
Click the plus and minus buttons for small steps.
Click File to open the menu for your whole document.
From there you can start a new document, open one, save, print and share.
Click the arrow at the top left of that menu to come back to your page.
Save often so you never lose your work. Click the Save icon.
The first time, Word asks for a name. Type a name you will remember, like Letter to Ade.
Choose where to keep it, then click Save. After that, the Save icon updates the same file.
